title: What to watch at the open
text: Yesterday was a big day. The S&P 500 fund SPY rose 1.7% to $766.81 and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ rose 1.0%. Microsoft jumped 6.7%, Amazon 6.1% and Intuitive Surgical 9.4%. But Vertiv fell 12.9% and Lockheed Martin fell 6.9%. Today, watch whether the big gainers hold their gains or give some back, and how AMD opens after its quarterly report on Tuesday evening. After a big jump, prices often calm down or swing the other way, so a quiet day would be normal too.

title: Big AI companies up, chip and equipment makers down
text: Microsoft closed at $555.80, just under its 52 week high of $559.15. Amazon gained 6.1% and Alphabet 3.2%. In the other group, NVIDIA fell 3.2%, TSMC 2.2% and Broadcom 2.0%. Think of it like a school team: the players who use the tools did well, while the companies that sell the tools had a harder day. Reports linked the rally to relief after the US midterm elections, but we could not confirm one single reason, so we only report the numbers.

title: Vertiv fell almost 13% in one day
text: Vertiv makes power and cooling equipment for data centers. It closed at $205.55, down 12.9%, on a day when volume was more than double its usual. On October 28 it reported sales up 61%, so this is another example of a stock falling after good news. We could not confirm the reason for the drop. Its price is now only 39% of the way up its 52 week range.

title: Lockheed Martin dropped almost 7%
text: Lockheed Martin is a defense company that usually moves slowly (its beta is only 0.1, which means it rarely follows the market). It closed at $595.04, down 6.9%, with trading volume more than double normal. We could not find a verified reason, so none is given here. Even calm companies can have rough days.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield is still high
text: The 10 year Treasury yield is the interest rate the US government pays to borrow money for ten years. Its monthly average was 5.13% in October, up from 4.06% a year earlier. When safe bonds pay more, some investors may choose them over stocks, so this number is worth watching.

title: Lesson 38: What is dividend yield?
text: Dividend yield tells you how much a company pays in dividends each year compared with its stock price. If a stock costs $100 and pays $2 a year, the yield is 2%. Today TSMC's yield is about 1.1%, Microsoft's is about 0.65%, and NVIDIA's is about 0.26%, so they pay little. SCHD, the fund built from steady dividend payers, holds companies that pay more. Here is the catch: the yield changes when the price changes. If a stock falls and the dividend stays the same, the yield goes up, but that is not a gift, because you just lost value in the price. A high yield can also be a warning sign that people doubt the company can keep paying. Yield is one clue, never the whole story.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices come from the market close on November 4. Analyst targets and ratios are available for NVIDIA, TSMC, AMD, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Lockheed Martin and GE only. Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical have price data but no analyst targets or ratios. Reasons for several price moves could not be verified. This is information to learn from, not advice to buy or sell.
